requirements.evidence: Every contract item is present: `Queues` with all required properties/public methods (`app/Livewire/Entity/Queues.php:64-218`), `Serve` with `selectedQueueId`/`mode`/`lastCalledTicketId`/`notice`/`callNext()` (`app/Livewire/Entity/Serve.php:39-110`), both routes (`routes/web.php:59-60`), and all required keys in both locales. Misses: the queue and mode selects use deferred `wire:model` (`resources/views/livewire/entity/serve.blade.php:13,23`), so the waiting list does not follow a selection, and several queue controls have no required aria-label (`resources/views/livewire/entity/queues.blade.php:14,48,79-80,86-91,111-113`).

conventions.evidence: Domain writes go through actions (`Queues.php:97,155-160,190,255`), Livewire validation uses `#[Validate]` + `validateOnly` (`Queues.php:29,57,94,152`; `Serve.php:50,85`), authorization goes through policies (`Queues.php:73,111,199,253`), and docs/CHANGELOG are updated (`CHANGELOG.md:12-15`; `docs/business-rules.md:105`). Deviations: manager detection is hardcoded in Blade (`queues.blade.php:137`), and PHPDoc is absent on the new public methods.

security.evidence: Foreign ids are consistently scoped (`Queues.php:109,131,148,172,186,197,250-251`; `Serve.php:82,149`), access data is scoped (`Queues.php:226-239`), `lastCalledTicketId` is `#[Locked]` (`Serve.php:56-57`), and all output uses `{{ }}`. Gap: `render()` (`Queues.php:220-241`) and close/cancel actions (`Queues.php:116-127,205-208`) do not re-authorize, so a demoted manager with an old snapshot can still read queues, memberships and grants by tampering with public properties.

tests.evidence: New Pest suites cover happy paths, validation, foreign-id tamper, locked properties, rate limiting and demotion (`tests/Feature/Entity/QueuesTest.php`, `ServeTest.php`, `MembersTabsTest.php`, `QueueNavigationTest.php`). Gaps: the demoted-manager test only exercises seven actions (`QueuesTest.php:336-371`), missing `create`, `openQueue` and `rename`, and there is no test that the waiting list hides tickets for a queue the user may not call (`ServeTest.php:101-137,244-258`).

simplicity.evidence: The change reuses existing `x-label`/`x-input`, the default layout and the domain Actions, and factors the repeated logic into `setAccess()` (`Queues.php:248-256`) and `firstValidationMessage()` (`Queues.php:261-264`). Minor repetition remains in the repeated title translation and nested view-data ternaries (`queues.blade.php:2,7,9`; `serve.blade.php:2,7,8`).

readability.evidence: Names are clear, methods are focused and the property docblocks explain the untrusted state. The nested ternaries in `render()` (`Queues.php:222-239`) and the role check embedded in the view (`queues.blade.php:137`) make those spots harder to follow than the rest of the change.

scope.evidence: Every hunk serves the task: the two components/views, routes and navbar entries, both language files, the members tabs, the required docs/CHANGELOG updates and the tests; no unrelated refactors or files.

issues.explanation: Livewire 3's `wire:model` is deferred, so changing the queue or mode select does not issue a request and the waiting list keeps showing the previously selected queue's tickets until another action; use `wire:model.live` on both selects.

`render()` and the close/cancel methods re-render without re-authorizing, so a demoted manager holding an old snapshot can set `accessQueueId`/`managingAccess` or simply call `closeQueue` and still read queue names, member names/emails and access grants; mount alone only guards the initial load.

The task requires aria-labels on interactive controls, but the queue row button, create cancel, rename cancel/submit, rename/deactivate/access launch buttons and toggle cancel/confirm buttons have none while only create/close/grant/revoke do.

The demoted-manager test omits `create`, `openQueue` and `rename` (and the render path), and there is no test that the waiting list hides tickets when the selected queue is one the user may not `call`, so the convention's per-action unauthorized/tamper coverage is incomplete.
The Blade decides who is a manager by hardcoding `UserRole::Owner`/`Admin`, duplicating the policy rule in the view instead of using an ability or a computed value.
The waiting list hides the priority tag for normal tickets (`priority` 0), although the task asks the list to show priority, code, issue time and channel.
The title translation is recomputed three times on each page and `Queues::render()` uses nested ternaries for the view data, which is avoidable repetition.

review.summary: The change adds the queues management page, the serve panel, members tabs and navigation, with entity-scoped lookups, delegation to the domain actions and broad feature tests. It is close to the task, but needs changes: the serve queue/mode selects use deferred `wire:model` so the waiting list is stale, several queue controls lack the required aria-labels, and `render()`/close actions do not re-authorize, letting a demoted manager keep reading. The security scoping and test coverage are otherwise strong.
